claims.access_scope: Publisher article text: abstract, structural comparison, functional analysis, discussion, and cloning sections; supplementary plots not inspected.
claims.claim: The E. coli AllD study reports NAD preference and a structural explanation involving Asp308/Gln309. The R48A and H116A mutants lacked measured activity. These are reference-enzyme observations, not Cannabis annotations.
claims.boundary: Does not establish reverse flux, a Cannabis homolog, or NADP activity. Residue conservation alone would not establish substrate specificity.

claims.claim: EC 1.1.1.350 separates the NAD-specific activity and lists reviewed reference proteins P58408 and P77555.
EC 1.1.1.154 includes both cofactor equations and describes dual activity in Arthrobacter allantoicus; it does not supply a reviewed sequence in this entry.

claims.access_scope: Indexed publisher abstract excerpt; direct page fetch failed; full paper not reviewed.
claims.claim: The Arthrobacter purification study reports conversion of S-ureidoglycolate to oxalurate using either NAD or NADP.
claims.boundary: No exact assayed-protein sequence has been resolved here. Do not equate a name or EC match with sequence-linked biochemical evidence.

decision: Preserve separate cofactor-specific gaps. Do not transfer the E. coli NAD reference assignment to the NADP equation.
next_tests: Resolve the assayed Arthrobacter strain and protein sequence from the original purification study before assigning a dual-cofactor reference.

For any future Cannabis lead, assay chemically verified S-ureidoglycolate and oxalurate with NAD/NADH and NADP/NADPH separately, using substrate-decay and no-protein controls and product identification.
Test both directions independently; an oxidation assay does not establish synthesis in the selected reverse route.
